actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 405 - 0 (Roll no. 43). (text: CR H737)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 405 - 0 (Roll no. 43). (text: CR H737)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H748)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 825.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H737-739)
Mr. Williams (TX) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.

dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals finally convicted of specific COVID-19 loan or grant fraud, and any small businesses associated with them.
dimensions.evidence: An associate of a small business concern who is finally convicted of any crime involving or relating to financial misconduct or a false statement with respect to a covered loan or grant shall be ineligible

dimensions.assessment: Denies all non-disaster SBA financial assistance to convicted individuals and their associated small business concerns.
dimensions.evidence: ineligible to receive any financial assistance from the Administrator, other than financial assistance under section 7(b).

dimensions.assessment: Restricts future federal financial assistance outlays for specified individuals and businesses, though specific dollar impacts are not detailed.
Amends section 16 of the Small Business Act to add a statutory financial assistance prohibition.
dimensions.evidence: Section 16 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 645) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to future SBA assistance for covered convictions, excluding existing contracts or agreements.
dimensions.evidence: shall not apply to any contract or other agreement entered into by the Government prior to the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The exact number of individuals or businesses that have been or will be convicted of the specified offenses is not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill prohibits individuals finally convicted of financial misconduct or false statements related to specific COVID-19 pandemic loans and grants, as well as the small businesses associated with them, from receiving future financial assistance from the Small Business Administration, excluding disaster loans.
